newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas continues to rise, Q3 posts biggest gain.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas continues to rise, Q3 posts biggest gain.

text.p: UK natural gas prices held the gains made on Thursday and went even higher in some periods on Friday, with the third quarter particularly strong, traders and brokers said.

The third quarter traded several times between 11.10 pence and 11.30 pence a therm. At one point it was bid at 11.25 pence and offers withdrew completely, but the market softened later to a range of 11.00/11.25 pence by the close, a broker said. By contrast, the quarter had traded at 10.70 pence on Thursday.

A seller at St Fergus, who sold some material for June there, said there appeared to be still a lot of requirements for the last part of June and for the whole of the third quarter, pushing up prices significantly. But he added that the volume of trade was not as high as on Thursday, saying "the panic element has been missing today."

The strength seen in Q1 on Thursday was also consolidated on Friday, with trade repeated at 17.00 pence a therm, the highest level it had reached on Thursday. One player agreed that the price had held up, but said he was not sure there were enough buyers looking for material to keep levels so high. "I suspect we may see a retracement some time next week," he said.

There was once again some interest for prompt gas, with several trades done for the weekend and on the within day market. Within day prices were stronger than the previous day, with trade done as high as 11.60 pence a therm at Bacton.
One trader said he thought there may have been several deals done on a private and confidential basis, but the market was clearly quieter than the previous day even as prices continued to rise.

The IPE market saw prices rise across the board, with February posting the biggest gain, of 0.40 pence a therm, to settle at 17.90 pence, at parity with January. Although 200 lots were traded, all were done in the morning, with no activity seen at all as interest faded away after lunch.

Transco forecasts the weather continuing to get milder, with Saturday's temperature set at 10.1 Celsius, up from 8.9 Celsius for Friday but still below the seasonal normal 12.3 Celsius. Demand is set to fall to 203 mcm on Saturday, 47 percent of peak day demand.
